prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1046; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision at low speed, and the claimant's representing attorney has asked that all contact go through their office.
Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage to the rear of the claimant's vehicle, and the damage is mostly in line with the impact described by the parties.
Entry 3: The police report and two parties at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time, though no independent witnesses were located.
Entry 4: The driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force on the date of loss, with nothing suggesting the damage predates coverage.
Entry 5: No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records, and the repair estimate was reviewed against the photos.
Entry 6: The claimant's neck strain was reported to the attorney's office, and the reported injury matches the kind and force of a crash of this type.
Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy tapering as the patient improved, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known from prior records.
Entry 8: The claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far, and the file is being prepared for a settlement review with the attorney's office.
